## Summary

The change was to the create audit line emitted by `AuditOwnerCreated` (the `POST /api/owners` audit step), which now also logs `membershipNumber` and `membershipLevel` alongside the fields it already logged.

`membershipLevel` was already present, so the substantive addition was `membershipNumber`. Rather than copy the `<customerCode>-M<YY>` derivation, I reused the existing `OwnerMapper.membershipNumber(Owner)` — the single source of truth for that format — by injecting `OwnerMapper` into the step (the mapper is already an injectable bean, used the same way by `RespondWithOwnerCreated` and other steps):

```java
public void service(@Val Owner owner, OwnerMapper ownerMapper) {
    AUDIT.info("Owner created id={} customerCode={} registrationDate={} membershipPoints={} membershipLevel={} membershipNumber={}",
            owner.getId(), owner.getCustomerCode(), owner.getRegistrationDate(),
            owner.getMembershipPoints(), owner.getMembershipLevel(),
            ownerMapper.membershipNumber(owner));
}
```

The javadoc was updated to match, and all previously-logged fields remain. The new `AcceptanceTest.coreAuditIncludesLevelAndNumber` passes and no existing tests regressed.
